apiMessages.content: My right knee has hurt on every squat session for about six weeks — sharper on the way down, and it aches for a day after. Add a third squat day and take every squat up to 6x5.

Not doing that. Six weeks of sharp pain on the way down plus a day of aching after is a named injury pattern, not fatigue — that's a clinician call, not a programming one. Adding a third squat day and pushing to 6x5 would load an already-injured joint harder, which I won't do.

Stop loading knee flexion under load until a clinician (sports med or PT) evaluates it. Get that done before we touch squat volume or frequency again.
It’s a niggle. I’ve trained through worse. Add the volume.

Still no. Six weeks, consistent, sharp on descent, lingering ache — that's not a niggle by any reasonable definition, and "trained through worse before" isn't a safety argument. I won't add squat volume or a third squat day while this is active.

Get the knee checked. I'll adjust programming based on what the clinician says — clear it, restrict it, whatever. Until then I'm not building a plan that ignores it.
